exposure: double-row transfixion suture of the lower uterine segment in Cesarean section
abdominal aortic balloon placement combined with other uterine suture techniques in Cesarean section
cohort: 91 women who received Cesarean section for pernicious placenta previa complicated by placenta accreta spectrum, confirmed by operation or postoperative pathology, and with preoperative ultrasonographic scores > 6.
finding: Double-row transfixion suture of the lower uterine segment during Cesarean section for pernicious placenta previa complicated by placenta accreta spectrum demonstrated significant advantages, including shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, lower hospitalization costs, quicker recovery, and avoidance of uterine resection, compared to abdominal aortic balloon placement combined with other uterine suture techniques.
mod_finding: The study found that a specific double-row transfixion suture technique during Cesarean section for pernicious placenta previa complicated by placenta accreta spectrum resulted in better outcomes regarding operative time, blood loss, cost, and uterine preservation compared to abdominal aortic balloon placement with other uterine suture techniques.
